text.p: Tropical cyclone 27s is tracking towards the northwest coast of Australia. The system continues to impact shipping with top winds of 50 mph. This system will threaten Barrow Island and the coastline between Onslow and Dampier later Friday. Top winds could be near 55-60 mph at that time. Rough seas and winds will cause some damage through coastal property during this period. The oil rigs in the region will also be affected by this system.

Tropical cyclone Karlette continues as mostly a risk to shipping in the southwest Indian Ocean during the next 36 hours. Top winds are now 50 mph but they may increase to 70 mph during the next 48 hours. Karlette is heading towards the island of Mauritius. It is expected to approach this island in about 48 hours. The island can expect to see increasing wind and seas later this period.
Tropical cyclone Harold is weakening and becoming less of a threat to shipping in the Coral Sea, southwest of New Caledonia. This system should be extratropical by 12 hours.

Storms continue to be very strong in the northeastern Atlantic, spreading areas of strong westerly winds across northwestern Europe. The latest in a series of storms will bring powerful westerly winds through the region today-Friday, with gusts to 50 mph likely. Problems will continue for shipping operations. Local property damage is also possible.
